study type: secondary analysis of a retrospective cohort study
exposure: neighbourhood socioeconomic position (economic hardship and inequality, financial strength and educational attainment)
cohort: 3012 individuals with Medicaid or private insurance who planned for permanent contraception postpartum
finding: Adequacy of prenatal care mediated the relationship between neighbourhood socioeconomic disadvantage and postpartum permanent contraception fulfilment, particularly for patients with Medicaid.
mod_finding: This study examined the relationship between neighborhood socioeconomic position and postpartum permanent contraception fulfillment but did not examine mode of delivery.
